description: Menu hung on a trigger you supply: keyboard navigation, portal and ARIA are built in, so spread `triggerProps` onto your own button. Items, sections and dividers are the parts. When the trigger is an ordinary labelled button, `<MenuButton>` is that already assembled — including the split form where a default action sits on its own half. Come here when the trigger is something else: an avatar, a table row, a field.

props.name: align
props.description: Which edge the menu lines up with, and it follows where the trigger SITS: the default `end` for a control at the right, `start` on the left, so the menu opens into the page and not off its edge.

props.name: menuClassName
props.description: Class on the menu element (portaled to body — needed for descendant selectors).

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description: Close menu when an item is clicked. Default true. Set false for multi-select.

props.name: matchTriggerWidth
props.description: Menu width: true = exactly the trigger's width (select-style), 'min' = at least the trigger's width but growing with longer content. Default false (intrinsic width).

props.name: triggerId
props.description: Name the trigger yourself instead of letting one be generated. Use it when something outside has to reach the control by id: `<Field htmlFor>`, or an `ErrorSummary` row that puts focus on the field it names.

example:
<Dropdown
  align="end"
  trigger={({ isOpen, ...triggerProps }) => (
    <Button data-open={isOpen || undefined} {...triggerProps}>
      Actions
      <Icon name="arrow_drop_down" />
    </Button>
  )}
>
  
  <DropdownSection label="Edit">
    <DropdownItem icon="edit" shortcut="⌘E" onClick={() => undefined}>Rename</DropdownItem>
    
    <Tooltip content="Only the owner can move this">
      <DropdownItem icon="folder" disabled>Move to folder</DropdownItem>
    </Tooltip>
  </DropdownSection>
  
  <DropdownDivider />
  <DropdownItem icon="delete" tone="danger" onClick={() => undefined}>Delete</DropdownItem>
</Dropdown>
